info.title: Mesub API
info.description:
Recurring payments on Solana, read and driven from your own server. This document is the contract of `/v1` and of the webhooks: what it does not name is not part of it.

## Calls

- Every route takes the project's API key as a bearer token, `Authorization: Bearer SUB_...`, and never in the query string. Everything is scoped to the project the key belongs to.
- Fields are in snake case, statuses and reasons in lowercase. Dates are ISO 8601 strings in UTC, with milliseconds. Token amounts are strings in the token's smallest unit, and so is every other integer that may not fit in a double (`last_valid_block_height`, lamports).
- A field nobody set is `null`, never left out, except where a field says otherwise (`reason` and `reason_code` on a confirmation, `attempts` on an access answer).
- A query or body field a route does not know is refused, `400 invalid_request`.
- Every answer, errors included, carries `Mesub-Request-Id`, the id Mesub gave the request (`req_` and 24 letters or digits). Log it beside your own; quote it to Mesub support to find the request in our logs. Mesub writes it: an id sent with the request is ignored.

## Versions

- Send `Mesub-Version` on every call to name the version of this contract your code is written against. The one version served today is `2026-10-02`.
- A call without the header is served as the first version, `2026-10-02`, for good: an integration written without it never changes under its feet.
- A value that is not, to the letter, a version this API serves (another date, `latest`, an empty header) is refused with `400 unsupported_version`, whose message lists the versions served. The API key and the rate limit are checked first: a wrong key reads `401` whatever version it names.
- Every answer under `/v1`, errors included, says in `Mesub-Version` the version it is written in: the one asked for, or `2026-10-02` when the call named none or one this API does not serve.

## Compatibility

- Within a version, this contract only grows. Without a new `Mesub-Version`, an answer may gain a field, an enum may gain a value, an answer may gain an error code, an attempt may gain a reason, a confirmation may gain a `reason_code`, and a webhook may gain an event type or a field. Your code must ignore what it does not know: never fail on an unknown field, and treat an unknown enum value, code, reason or event as "something else".
- Anything else takes a new version: removing or renaming a field, changing its type or its meaning, making an optional request field required, or changing the status of an error.
- Before the first integrator, exceptions were made once, in this version: values moved to snake case (an attempt's `reason`, for example `insufficient_balance` and `program_4`), and each fact got one word: the codes `plan_deleted` and `plan_rebuilt` become `plan_removed` and `plan_replaced`, an attempt's `plan_gone`, `delegation_gone` and `subscription_cancelled` become `plan_removed`, `closed_elsewhere` and `cancelled`, and `end_reason` `authority_closed` becomes `closed_elsewhere`; and webhook bodies took the shape of an event (see Webhooks).

## Rate limits

- Counted per API key, per route, over a minute: 1,000 calls to the routes that read, 60 to the routes that build a transaction, read the chain or write (each route says its own in `x-mesub.limit`). A call without a valid key is counted against its IP, 120 a minute.
- Counted in the memory of the server that answers: the limits are a floor, not a promise of what gets through.
- `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds) come on every answer the limit counted. Past the limit: `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`, in seconds.

## Errors

- Every error under `/v1` answers the same body: `statusCode`, `error` (the status's name), `code`, `message`, `retryable` and `request_id`. `message` is a sentence for a person, or a list of them when the body or the query failed validation; it may be reworded any day.
- Branch on `code`. A code is never moved to another status or reused for another cause, and is renamed only in a new version (see Compatibility). The codes each answer may carry are listed under it, in `x-codes`.
- `retryable` says whether the same request, sent again unchanged, may succeed later. `Retry-After`, when present, says how long to wait.
- Beside what each route lists: a path or a method that does not exist answers `404 not_found`; a body over 100 kB answers `413 payload_too_large`; a fault of ours answers `500 internal_error`, retryable, since every route is safe to call twice.

## Webhooks

- Each delivery is a `POST` of a JSON body, `{ id, object, type, created_at, network, api_version, sequence, data, detail }`: `id` is the event's, `sequence` its place among the subscription's events, `data` the subscription as it stood right after the change that raised this event, as [Retrieve a subscription](/reference/subscriptions/retrieve) would have answered it then, and `detail` what the event is about. A delivery sent by hand from the dashboard also carries `test: true`.
- `data` is the subscription as it stood right after the change that raised this event; events raised by the same change share it, and `detail` says what each event is about. A last retry that fails raises `subscription.payment_failed` and `subscription.stopped`, both showing `status: stopped`; the failure's cause is in `payment_failed`'s `detail`. Do not assume the order events arrive in: apply a subscription's events in the order of their `sequence` (1, 2, 3...), skipping one lower than the last you applied, or read [Retrieve a subscription](/reference/subscriptions/retrieve) for the state now. An event without `sequence` (one written before Mesub numbered events, or one it could not number) cannot be placed: read the subscription's state now rather than applying its `data`.
- Access: `subscription.access_granted` and `subscription.access_revoked` are sent exactly when the access a subscription grants changes (`data.access`), whatever made it change, a date passing included. `detail.changed_at` is when access changed (a date that passed, to the millisecond, even when the event is written seconds or hours later), and the moment `data` describes; `created_at` is when Mesub wrote the event, never before an event written earlier, so [List events](/reference/events/list) serves it in the order it was written. One event per change, never two. Drive your customer's access from these two: `sequence` orders one subscription's events, the access of the highest one applied stands; the other events say why. A renewal paid on time, or a resume while the paid period runs, changes nothing and sends neither. `detail.blocked_reason` and `detail.access_until` say whether the charges were held then, and when access ended or ends.
- Transitions: a cancellation that reached its end sends `subscription.ended` (`end_reason: cancelled`, `detail.changed_at` its expiry) once the chain shows the cancellation still in place past its expiry, after the `subscription.access_revoked` of that expiry; a resume seen late can still follow an `access_revoked`; a seat parked over the project's subscriber limit sends `subscription.paused`, and `subscription.unpaused` when it is back. Each once per change, ordered by `sequence` beside the access events. `subscription.created` carries its first payment in `detail.first_payment`.
- [List events](/reference/events/list) serves the same bodies, byte for byte once parsed, over the last 30 days: catch up there on what an endpoint missed.
- Bodies written before `available_since` (see [List events](/reference/events/list)), and the few written during the deploy that brought this shape by a server still on the previous version, keep the shape they were sent in: `{ type, created_at, data }`, with `detail` inside `data`, no `id`, and `data` as it was at the delivery's first attempt. A retry or a resend of one sends it unchanged.
- An event whose capture failed is held: its deliveries are not sent and it is missing from [List events](/reference/events/list) until Mesub recovers it. Mesub is alerted, and never sends or serves an event with a later state.
- Signed the Standard Webhooks way: `webhook-signature` is `v1,` and the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `webhook-id.webhook-timestamp.body`, keyed with the endpoint's secret (the part after `whsec_`, base64 decoded). Check it over the raw bytes received.
- The header may list several signatures, space separated. When an endpoint's secret is regenerated with an overlap (up to 24 hours, chosen then), the old secret keeps signing beside the new one until the overlap ends: every attempt in that window carries two, the new secret's first, and an attempt after it, a retry included, carries the new one alone. Verify against each and accept the delivery when any one matches; the Standard Webhooks libraries and `@mesub/node` do.
- `webhook-id` names the delivery: one per event and per endpoint, the same on every retry of it and on a resend from the dashboard. Deduplicate on it. Two endpoints of a project receiving one event get two ids.
- The body is written once, at the event's first attempt, and every retry and every endpoint gets the same bytes; `webhook-timestamp` is the attempt's own.
- Answer with a 2xx within 10 seconds. Anything else, a redirect included, is a failure: the delivery is tried again 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes and 2 hours later, then every 12 hours, eleven attempts over about three days. An endpoint that fails for three days with no success in between is turned off.

## What may change without a new version

Without a new `Mesub-Version`, Mesub may add:

- fields to an answer or to a webhook body;
- values to an enum (a `status`, a reason, an `outcome`), and to the open families that are not enums (an attempt's `reason`);
- error codes, to any route;
- webhook events;
- optional parameters and optional body fields.

Your code must ignore a field it does not know, and keep a default branch on every enum, reason and code. Anything else, renaming or removing a field, changing its type or its meaning, making something optional required, takes a new version, and the versions already served keep answering as they did.

Decided before the first integrator, and made without a new version:

- reasons and `detail` values move to snake case (`insufficient-balance` becomes `insufficient_balance`, `program:4` becomes `program_4`, `grace-ended` becomes `retry_deadline_passed`);
- the error code `plan_deleted` becomes `plan_removed`, and `plan_rebuilt` becomes `plan_replaced`, the words `end_reason` already uses;
- an attempt's `reason` takes the word `end_reason` uses for the same fact: `plan_gone` becomes `plan_removed`, `subscription_cancelled` becomes `cancelled`, and `delegation_gone` becomes `closed_elsewhere`;
- `end_reason` `authority_closed` becomes `closed_elsewhere`, the subscription account closed outside Mesub: `authority_closed` names only the subscription authority closed for good, as `late_reason` does;
- a webhook body gains `id`, `object`, `network` and `api_version`, `detail` moves out of `data` to the top, and `data` describes the subscription at the event rather than at the first attempt. Bodies written before `available_since` keep their shape.

`network` keeps `mainnet-beta`: the name Solana gives its cluster.

get.description:
Whether a customer may use a plan, and what explains the answer. Always 200 for a customer, subscribed or not: a customer who never subscribed answers `access: false` with `status: "none"`. The 404 is about the slug, never about them.

Leave `plan` out to get every plan of the project the customer has anything on.

On a plan with an end date, nobody has access past that date: `access` is false from the plan's end on and `access_until` is never later, whatever period was paid for. The subscription turns `ended` within minutes of it, so `status` can still read `active` or `unpaid` for that long with `access` false. Gate on `access`.

A charge may be held for a reason that is not the customer's: the answer then carries `blocked_since` and `blocked_reason`, both null otherwise. `status` and `payment_status` stay as they were, and Mesub keeps trying. `access` is never true past `access_until` on a blocked subscription. [Lifecycle](/docs/lifecycle#blocked-charges) says what each reason asks of you.

post.description:
Reserves a subscription to one of your plans for the wallet named, and builds what that wallet signs: the terms, as a message, then the transaction, without sending it. Hand both to [Submit](/reference/subscriptions/submit).

The transaction lives 150 blocks, about half a minute: `transaction_expires_at` estimates when they run out, `last_valid_block_height` says it. The terms live five minutes. Have the terms signed first, then ask for [a fresh transaction](/reference/subscriptions/transaction) when the wallet is ready to sign it.

Called again for the same plan, wallet and customer while nothing has landed, it answers the same subscription with a fresh transaction. The customer is the `external_id`, else the `email`, else nobody. Another customer naming the same wallet gets a subscription of its own: only the one the wallet signs for lands.

A wallet whose subscription to this plan stopped comes back over its existing authorisation: a new subscription, with `costs.rent` at zero.

On a plan with an end date, `terms.message` says that the last charge is in full and that access stops when the plan ends. When the plan ends before a second charge can be made, it says the charge is a single one.

post.description:
A fresh transaction for a subscription still waiting for its signature, with the terms it names. A transaction lives 150 blocks, about half a minute: `transaction_expires_at` estimates when they run out, `last_valid_block_height` says it. The terms live five minutes. So have the terms signed first, and call this route when the wallet is ready for the transaction: its 150 blocks start here, not while the customer reads. Have the wallet sign it at once, then send it with the terms signature to [Submit](/reference/subscriptions/submit). Always sign the transaction of the last call.

To know whether a terms signature you hold is still good, compare `terms.message` with the message the wallet signed. The same text is the same terms: submit with the signature you hold. Another text is new terms: have the wallet sign this message, since submit refuses the old signature with `invalid_terms_signature`.

The terms come back unchanged while they have more than two minutes left before `terms.expires_at`. New terms come after that, after a submit that spent them (one answered `transaction_expired` may have), or when the plan changed on chain.

This route reserves nothing and takes no body: the wallet, the plan and the customer are the subscription's own. For a subscription that expired, call [Create](/reference/subscriptions/create) again.

post.description:
Relays what the wallet signed: the transaction and the terms. Mesub checks both signatures, co-signs, sends the transaction and waits for the chain, so this call is slow by design: up to 90 seconds.

Safe to send again unchanged. Mesub recognises what it already co-signed and answers from the chain, so a customer is never charged twice.

A transaction submitted after its 150 blocks, about half a minute, is refused with `transaction_expired`: nothing was sent, and the same submit sent again cannot land. Ask for [a fresh transaction](/reference/subscriptions/transaction), have the wallet sign it, and sign the terms again if their message changed.

post.description:
Runs the charge of the missed period now, rather than at its next retry: for a customer who topped up their wallet and wants their access back from your page. Nothing to sign: the wallet approved the plan when it subscribed.

The charge runs in the background, with the checks and records of a scheduled one. The answer is the subscription, still `unpaid`: the outcome comes as `subscription.renewed` or `subscription.payment_failed`, and on the subscription.

Refused before anything is queued when it cannot succeed, as the chain reads now, so that it never spends a retry for nothing: the wallet holds less than the period costs, no longer approves the subscription, or its token account is frozen, or the last charge found its authorisation closed.

On Free, a retry by hand is one of the missed period's three, whoever makes it, at least ten minutes apart, and none within two minutes of the end of the missed period. On Dev and Business it runs beside the schedule, and the wait between two doubles.

parameters.name: webhook-id
parameters.description: The delivery's id: one per event and per endpoint, the same on every retry of that delivery and on a resend from the dashboard. Deduplicate on it. Two endpoints receiving one event get two ids.

parameters.name: webhook-timestamp
parameters.description: When this attempt was sent, in Unix seconds: new on every retry, and signed with the body. Refuse one too far from your own clock.

parameters.name: webhook-signature
parameters.description: `v1,` then the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `webhook-id.webhook-timestamp.body`, keyed with the endpoint's signing secret (the part after `whsec_`, base64 decoded), the Standard Webhooks way. It may hold several, space separated: two while a regenerated secret's overlap runs, the new secret's first. Accept the delivery when any one matches your secret. Check it over the raw bytes received, before parsing them.

id.description: The event's id: the same in every delivery of it, to every endpoint and on every retry, and on [Retrieve an event](/reference/events/retrieve). `webhook-id` names the delivery, not the event.

created_at.description: When the event happened: the moment `data` describes.

network.description: The Solana network the subscription is on.

api_version.description: The version of this contract `data` and `detail` are written in, as `Mesub-Version` names them. Set when the body is written, and kept with it.

sequence.description: Its place among the events of this subscription: 1, 2, 3... in the order they happened, two events of one change included. Deliveries may arrive in any order: apply a subscription's events in the order of `sequence`, and skip one lower than the last you applied for it. Absent on bodies written before Mesub numbered events, and on an event it could not number. An event without `sequence` cannot be placed: read the subscription's state now, with [Retrieve a subscription](/reference/subscriptions/retrieve) or [Check access](/reference/access/check), rather than applying its `data`.

data.description: The subscription as it stood right after the change that raised this event, as [Retrieve a subscription](/reference/subscriptions/retrieve) would have answered it then, however late the delivery. Events raised by the same change share it, and `detail` says what each event is about: a last retry that fails raises `subscription.payment_failed` and `subscription.stopped`, both showing `status: stopped`, the failure's cause in `payment_failed`'s `detail`.

previous_id.description: On a comeback only: the id of the stopped subscription this one took over, now `superseded`. Absent otherwise.

first_payment.description: The first payment, the transfer the subscriber's own transaction carried. Null when Mesub recorded none at the confirmation: the subscription landed in a period paid only in part, which the next charge collects. Absent on events written before Mesub told it.

amount.description: What was paid, in the token's smallest unit.

signature.description: The signature of the transaction that paid it.

test.description: True on a test delivery of this event, sent by hand from the dashboard. Absent otherwise.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else, a redirect included, counts as a failure and is retried.

post.description:
A renewal is near, and whether it can pay.

Sent once per period, when the subscription enters the last quarter of it and three days before the charge at most, whether the charge can pay or not. Mesub reads the customer's wallet at that moment: `detail` is that reading, not a promise, and the charge itself answers with `subscription.renewed` or `subscription.payment_failed`. post.description:
A seat was parked: the project now holds more subscribers than its tier allows (it moved to a smaller tier, or a subscription confirmed late filled it), and Mesub stopped charging the newest ones rather than any within the limit. Not a pause the subscriber asked for: nothing changed on chain, and the status stays as it was.

The subscription keeps access to the end of the period it paid for, and no further: `data.paused` is true, `data.next_charge_at` null. Its `subscription.access_revoked` comes when that access ends, or right after this event, with a higher `sequence`, when it had already ended. The project moving back to a tier with room sends `subscription.unpaused`.

Mesub posts this to every endpoint of the project subscribed to it. Answer with a 2xx within 10 seconds.

AccessAnswer.description: Whether the customer has access to the plan, and what explains the answer.

wallet.description: The wallet the answer is about. Asked by `wallet`, that wallet. Asked by `external_id` or `email`, the one that pays, or null when the customer has nothing on this plan.

subscription_id.description: The subscription this answer is about: the one whose `status`, `access` and dates these are. Use it to [cancel](/reference/subscriptions/cancel), [resume](/reference/subscriptions/resume), [close](/reference/subscriptions/close) or [retry](/reference/subscriptions/retry) it without listing the customer's subscriptions first. When the customer has several on the plan, the one in force: among their wallets, the most recent that grants access, else the most recent; on one wallet, its latest, never a checkout left pending beside a subscription that runs, nor one left to expire. Null when the customer has nothing on this plan, with `status` `none`.

access.description: The only field a guard needs. False from the plan's end date on, whatever period was paid for.

status.description: Where the subscription stands. `none` for a customer who never subscribed to this plan. Mesub may add a status later: keep a default branch. For a few minutes after a plan's end date it can still read `active` or `unpaid` with `access` false, never `ended` with `access` true: gate on `access`.

paused.description: True on a seat parked over the project's subscriber limit: the status stays as it was, nothing is charged, and access runs to the end of the period already paid.

end_reason.description: Why it ended. Set only when `status` is `ended`. Null on every other status, and on an old subscription that ended with no reason recorded.

late_reason.description: Why a payment is late, as the last failed charge found it. Set only when `status` is `unpaid`, or `stopped` for the payment it stopped on. Null on every other status, and when Mesub cannot name the cause.

stop_reason.description:
Why it stopped. Set only when `status` is `stopped`. Null on every other status, and on a subscription that stopped before Mesub recorded why.

- `out_of_retries`: every retry of the missed payment failed. The subscription stays open on Solana: the subscriber can come back, or cancel it and close it once the period ends.
- `retry_deadline_passed`: on the Free tier, the last day to pay the missed payment passed.
- `authority_closed`: the wallet closed the account that lets Mesub charge it, for good. Nobody can charge this subscription again, and the subscriber cannot come back on it. They can close it now (`closable`) to get its deposit back.

payment_status.description: `late` while a charge missed and a retry is pending. `none` where nothing is being billed.

blocked_since.description: Since when every charge of this subscription is held for a reason that is not the customer's. Null when none is. `status` and `payment_status` do not change for it, and Mesub keeps trying. `access` ends at `access_until`, and comes back with the first charge that goes through, with nothing for the customer to sign.

blocked_reason.description: Why the charges are held. Null with `blocked_since`. Five values name the plan's own setup, yours to fix: `puller_not_allowed` (Mesub's puller was taken off the plan on chain), `receiver_not_allowed` (the receiving wallet is not among the plan's destinations), `receiver_account_missing` (it has no account for the plan's token, and nobody else can be paid), `receiver_account_frozen` (its account for the plan's token is frozen) and `mint_gone` (the token no longer exists). `mesub` is any cause on Mesub's side: nothing for you to fix. Mesub may add a value: keep a default branch.

subscribed_since.description: The start of the current subscription.

first_subscribed_at.description: The start of the very first one. Differs for a customer who left and came back.

current_period_end.description: The end of the period last paid for.

cancelled_at.description: When they asked to stop, not when access ends.

access_until.description: When access ends unless a charge renews it. Never later than the plan's end date, where access stops for everybody. Null while `access` is false. On a subscription whose charges are blocked (`blocked_since`), the date access ends if nothing is collected by then: the end of the period after the one paid for, or sooner when the cause is the plan's setup, the end of the grace the plan gives a late payment.

closable.description: Whether the subscriber can close the subscription on Solana now, which returns its deposit to their wallet: a cancellation whose end has passed, a subscription that ended with its plan, or one stopped with `stop_reason` `authority_closed`. As Mesub last knew the chain: the close reads the chain again, and may still be refused.

closable_from.description: When the subscriber can close it, if not now: the end of the period a cancellation set. Null when `closable` is true, and when no date is known yet: a running subscription, or one stopped with `out_of_retries`, must be cancelled first. As Mesub last knew the chain, like `closable`.

next_charge_at.description: The next charge. Null when a retry is pending instead, and when the plan's end date leaves no charge to make: a subscription in its last period has none.

next_retry_at.description: The next retry of a missed charge. Null when the plan ends before it.

retry_deadline.description: On Free only: when retries by hand close for the missed period, or the plan's end date when that comes first.

attempts.description: The last charges, newest first, five at most. Present only when asked with `attempts=true`.

reason_code.description:
Why, for a program: present exactly when `reason` is. Stable and in snake case, never reworded. An open family rather than a closed list: Mesub adds codes without a new version, so keep a default branch. Known today:

- `not_our_transaction`: the signature is not of a transaction Mesub co-signed over terms the wallet signed for this subscription.
- `transaction_failed`: the transaction landed and the chain refused it: nothing it held happened.
- `transaction_expired`: its blockhash ran out before it landed: it never will.
- `nothing_landed`: on a submit, no subscription stands at its address yet: it stays `pending`.
- `subscription_not_on_chain`: on a cancel or a resume, the subscription no longer exists on chain.
- `subscription_mismatch`: what landed names another wallet, plan, amount or billing period than the subscription reserved, which is now `failed`.
- `dev_not_running`: Mesub's own Dev plan landed cancelled or part paid, and is now `failed`.
- `earlier_subscription_running`: a comeback paid while the subscription it came back over ran again: Mesub was told and sorts it out.
- `subscription_remade`: on a submit, it landed, and the subscription was closed and made again without Mesub since: now `failed`.
- `cancellation_not_landed`: the subscription stands on chain with no cancellation.
- `resume_not_landed`: the subscription stands on chain still cancelled.
- `close_not_landed`: the subscription still stands on chain.
- `subscription_changed`: the subscription moved on while the cancellation was read, and was left as it is.
- `subscription_not_cancelled`: on a resume, the subscription is no longer cancelled: nothing to resume.
- `cancelled_subscription_remade`: on a resume, the subscription cancelled was closed and made again without Mesub since: it stays `cancelled`.
- `resume_unverified`: on a resume, the subscription on chain cannot be told to be the one cancelled: it stays `cancelled`.

transaction.description: Base64, signed by nobody. The subscription's own wallet signs and sends it.

last_valid_block_height.description: The block height after which the transaction can no longer land.

transaction_expires_at.description: When `last_valid_block_height` is expected to pass: an estimate, about half a minute after the answer. Mesub reads it from how fast block heights went (skipped slots included), taking the faster of the last half hour and the last 30 seconds, and counts the blocks the chain's tip is ahead of what it read, so the estimate errs early, not late, while the chain keeps its pace. The height is the truth: rebuild the transaction when the chain refuses it with an expired blockhash, before this time as after it. Use this for a countdown, or to ask for a fresh transaction before it runs out.

Event.description: An event about a subscription: the very body its webhooks carry.

id.description: The event's id, the one its webhook bodies carry.

type.description: The event's name, as its webhook is named.

created_at.description: When the event happened: the moment `data` describes, but for an access event or a cancellation reaching its end, written when Mesub wrote the event, whose `detail.changed_at` is that moment.

network.description: The Solana network the subscription is on.

api_version.description: The version of this contract `data` and `detail` are written in, as `Mesub-Version` names them. Set when the body is written, and kept with it.

sequence.description: Its place among the events of this subscription: 1, 2, 3... in the order they happened, two events of one change included. Deliveries may arrive in any order: apply a subscription's events in the order of `sequence`, and skip one lower than the last you applied for it. Absent on bodies written before Mesub numbered events, and on an event it could not number. An event without `sequence` cannot be placed: read the subscription's state now, with [Retrieve a subscription](/reference/subscriptions/retrieve) or [Check access](/reference/access/check), rather than applying its `data`.

data.description: The subscription as it stood right after the change that raised this event, as [Retrieve a subscription](/reference/subscriptions/retrieve) would have answered it then, however late the delivery. Events raised by the same change share it, and `detail` says what each event is about: a last retry that fails raises `subscription.payment_failed` and `subscription.stopped`, both showing `status: stopped`, the failure's cause in `payment_failed`'s `detail`.

detail.description: The event's own fields, as its webhook describes them under `detail`.

available_since.description: When Mesub began keeping events in this form. Events before it are not served, whatever the window: their webhooks carried the older shape.

MesubVersion.name: Mesub-Version
MesubVersion.description: The version of this contract the call is written against. Without it, the call is served as the first version, `2026-10-02`. Any other value is refused with `400 unsupported_version`.
The version the answer is written in: the one asked for, or `2026-10-02` when the call named none, or one this API does not serve.

MesubRequestId.description: The id Mesub gave this request, on every answer, errors included, and in `request_id` on an error body. Quote it to Mesub support to find the request in our logs. Written by Mesub on each request: one sent with the request is ignored.

RateLimitLimit.description: The calls this route allows the API key in a minute, or the IP of a call without a valid key. Sent on every answer the rate limit counted.

RateLimitRemaining.description: What is left of them in the current minute.

RateLimitReset.description: Seconds until the count starts again.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before sending the same request again.

RetryAfterWithSomeCodes.description: Seconds to wait before sending the same request again. Sent with the codes that ask to wait: their `when` says so.
